component.name: Fretwork
component.summary: Play every track of a tab as its own stem

description.p: Fretwork is a tablature program for Linux that treats a score as a multitrack session. It reads Guitar Pro files, converts them to a format of its own, and renders each track through a separate synthesised instrument — so a track can be soloed, sent through its own amplifier simulation, and exported as an independent audio file.

That last part is the reason the program exists. Linux already has a tablature editor. What it has not had is a tablature program that gives you one synth per track, per-track LV2 effects, and real stems out the other end.

ul.li: Open a Guitar Pro file and draw the tablature, with the bar being played lit up as it goes
Give every track its own synthesiser, so solo and mute take effect while it plays
Let you edit — fret entry, rhythm, bars, selection, copy and paste, undo, transposition, tuning and capo
Export one audio file per track, wet or dry, or a backing track with a part removed
Tune your instrument from the audio input

description.p: Where a score asks for something Fretwork cannot honestly play, it says so rather than approximating it. The list of what those things are is in the documentation, and it is short and getting shorter.
"Guitar Pro" is a trademark of Arobas Music. Fretwork is not affiliated with them, not derived from their software, and ships none of their soundbanks or artwork.

description.p: Notes can be recorded from a MIDI keyboard against the transport, a bar at a time and one undo per bar, with the rule for where a note lands written down and tested.
The effects menu is in the order the signal goes, from dynamics to reverb, so a rig is built by reading down it.
A security review before this release closed a crash on crafted files, a fault in the plugin host, and a hole in the build pipeline; what a downloaded file can reach is now stated and small.
Slides, vibrato, tremolo picking and harmonics are played, drawn and exported. A harmonic sounds where a harmonic sounds, rather than at the pitch of the note under the finger.
A score can be written as MusicXML, which is the way to open it in another program.
A practice pack now carries the notation as well as the performance, and a file from an older Guitar Pro is named rather than merely refused.
The score is a document of real pages now, with a zoom and a page count, and the lines it is drawn with all appear.
Fretwork works out what key a piece is in from its notes, draws that key on a fretboard over the score, and writes the chords of any key into it from a circle of fifths.
A MIDI controller can drive the transport, the mixer and the knobs of a part's amplifier chain, and notes can be typed in from a keyboard.
Effect chains can be reordered and saved under a name, and a score can be written out as a fee[dB]ack practice pack.
First release. A tablature editor and player with per-track synthesis and stem export. Per-track LV2 chains and SFZ sampling are present and experimental.
